talk: FundBun · 2026 FinTechathon final round (29 Nov 2026, Shenzhen) · International AI Track · Topic A · 14 slides for a 15-minute pitch (about 14:10 spoken, 50 seconds in reserve) and 5 minutes of questions · positioning: today FundBun is a monitor, coach and friend that touches no external bank account; active money execution is the WeBank proposal on slide 13 and is verified in a local sandbox

slides.title: Introducing FundBun.
slides.alt: Title slide: Introducing FundBun. An AI money buddy that turns your spending into the dreams you want, and keeps you on track to reach them. On the right, a gold Dream Mirror shows a cracked Birkin 25 (¥98,000); beside it a furious, bright red Bun with a speech bubble that says 'You could've gotten a Birkin!'. 2026 FinTechathon Finalist, International AI Track, 29 Nov 2026, Shenzhen. Topic A: Personal Finance Assistant. Team lead Odri Prince Sembiring (Universitas Gadjah Mada); teammate Nadine Griselda (Universitas Airlangga).
slides.notes:
[0:00 to 0:35 · 35 s] Good morning. This is FundBun, and this is Bun. Bun is furious, because Jing overspent this month, and Bun is telling her exactly what it cost: 'You could've gotten a Birkin!' FundBun is an AI money buddy that turns your spending into the dreams you want, and keeps you on track to reach them. I'm Odri from Universitas Gadjah Mada. My teammate Nadine from Universitas Airlangga could not travel, so I am presenting for both of us.

Pacing: 14 slides, about 14 minutes, 50 seconds in reserve. If the clock is tight, shorten slides 5 and 10 first. Never cut slide 6: it sets the honest frame for everything after it.

slides.title: People stay on track with a carrot and a stick.
slides.alt: Why we made FundBun. Two cards. The carrot: see what you want get closer; stay disciplined and you watch your real dream move nearer, day by day (a whole Dream Mirror with a happy Bun, Birkin 25 closer). The stick: feel it the moment you stray; overspend and you see the dream slip away while Bun reacts on the spot (a cracked Dream Mirror with a furious Bun, Birkin 25 plus 5 weeks). The evidence behind it: 'Budgets speak in numbers, and numbers don't hurt.' d = 0.22 across 39 studies of opportunity-cost neglect (Maguire et al. 2023). Minus 19.6% monthly spend with a warning at the point of spending (Alipay's Huabei bill assistant).
slides.notes:
[0:35 to 1:30 · 55 s] Why did we make it? Because of the oldest idea in behaviour change: a carrot and a stick. People stay on track when they can see what they want getting closer. That is the carrot: stay disciplined and you watch your real dream move nearer. And they stay on track when they feel the consequence of straying, right away. That is the stick: overspend, and you see the dream slip away while Bun reacts on the spot. Budgeting apps miss both, because budgets speak in numbers, and numbers don't hurt. The research backs it. Across 39 studies people neglect what a purchase displaces. And when Alipay's Huabei warned people at the point of spending, monthly spend fell by 19.6 percent.

Q&A: 'Is the effect big enough?' The pooled effect is small (d = 0.22), which is why FundBun does not rely on one nudge: it pairs the mirror with tripwires, Bun's mood and a daily check-in. 'Is the stick shaming?' The stick is for the spending, never for logging it, and the tone is the user's choice.

slides.title: How FundBun keeps you on track, every day.
slides.alt: Four mechanisms: Dream Mirror, Tripwires, Daily Check-In streak, Category tracking. A mood ladder shows six drawings of Bun getting visibly angrier: Happy (money left over), Calm (on track), Worried (heading over), Angry (past your target), Furious (way past it), Burnt (toasted). The daily cool-down loop in three steps. You stray: the Dream Mirror cracks, the dream moves weeks away, and Bun heats up. You open it daily: a 7-day check-in streak earns a golden bun; log good days within your daily allowance. Bun cools down step by step: every 2 good days take one step off, and back within target the mirror mends. Right: Jing's home screen, past her target, with a zoom on the cracked mirror: Birkin 25 plus 5 weeks.
slides.notes:
[1:30 to 2:40 · 70 s] Here is how that works every day. Four things keep you on track: the Dream Mirror, tripwires, a daily check-in streak and category tracking. Now watch Bun. Bun's face is one ladder computed from your ledger: happy when there is money left over, calm when you are on track, worried when you are heading over, angry when you pass your target, furious when you are way past it, and finally burnt. On the right is Jing. She is past her target, so her Dream Mirror has cracked and her Birkin moved about five weeks further away. And here is the loop that brings people back. To calm Bun down and mend the mirror, you have to open the app every day and actually change how you spend. Log good days within your daily allowance, and Bun cools down step by step: every two good days take one step off. Check in seven days in a row and you earn a golden bun. Going quiet does not work: a day with nothing logged never calms Bun.

Q&A: 'Can I cheat by not logging?' No. Empty days are skipped, and three empty days end the streak. 'What is the daily allowance?' Your own daily tripwire if you set one, otherwise an even share of what is left to spend. 'Is Burnt a separate step?' The live ladder is five heat levels, happy to furious; burnt is the toasted face kept for older saved cards.

slides.title: Tripwires: cross a line you set, and Bun shows what it costs.
slides.alt: Tripwires, the crux. You set four kinds: 80% or 100% of target, a category limit, a single purchase over an amount you choose, and projected overspend. Crossing one shows a tangible reminder: 'Whoa, ¥1,299 at JD.com. That ¥1,299 = 1.3% of your Birkin 25.' Bun's tone is your choice: Gentle (default), Cheeky (opt-in) or Just numbers. Shame backfires (Gladstone et al. 2021), so the blunt voice is opt-in.
slides.notes:
[2:40 to 3:25 · 45 s] Tripwires are the stick at the moment of spending. You set the lines: 80 or 100 percent of your target, a category limit, any single purchase over an amount you choose, or a projected overspend. Cross one and Bun reminds you with something tangible. Here, ¥1,299 is 1.3 percent of Jing's Birkin. Shame backfires in the research, so you choose Bun's voice: gentle is the default, cheeky is opt-in, or just numbers.

Q&A: 'Who sets the rules?' The user, always. The agent can suggest a tripwire; it cannot weaken one silently.

slides.title: The product today: one core, a desktop app and a phone app.
slides.alt: The product today. Desktop app for Mac, Windows and Linux: an Electron shell and a local server on 127.0.0.1, with AI keys encrypted by the macOS Keychain on a Mac. Mobile-ready web and installable PWA app: the same core in the browser, with offline use after the first load. Dual Mode: Daily tracking for a simple count, or Goal and Mirror for the full Dream Mirror. Customizable dashboard blocks: move, resize or hide every card; the Daily check-in is movable and resizable too. Screenshots: the desktop dashboard and the phone home screen.
slides.notes:
[3:25 to 4:15 · 50 s] This is what exists today. One TypeScript core runs in two places. On a Mac, Windows or Linux computer it is an Electron desktop app with a local server that only listens on this computer. In a browser or on a phone it is the same core as a mobile-ready web app. On Android, Chrome can install it as a PWA on the Home Screen, and the first online load saves it for offline use. There are two modes: Daily tracking if you just want a simple count, and Goal and Mirror for the full Dream Mirror. And the dashboard is yours: every block can be moved, resized or hidden, the Daily check-in included.

Q&A: 'Is there a native mobile app?' No. Android gets an installable PWA, not an APK, and the payment-notification listener is still a roadmap item. 'Which desktop builds are tested?' The Mac app has been launched and its signature checked. Windows and Linux packages exist and have built on native CI runners, but still need launch tests on those operating systems.

slides.title: A monitor and a friend, not a bank.
slides.alt: What FundBun is today. FundBun watches your spending, coaches you and keeps you company; it never touches an external bank account. Monitor, keeps track of spending: manual entry, receipt X-ray, CSV import, read-only IMAP email receipts, file and folder analysis. Coach, gamifies discipline: Dream Mirror, escalating Bun mood, daily check-in streaks, tripwires, recovery plans. Friend, builds a daily habit: a reason to open it every day; Gentle, Cheeky or Just numbers; you confirm every entry; works with zero AI; no external bank account touched. Callout: active money execution (transfers, bill pay, subscription cancel) is pitched as part of the WeBank partnership, slide 13, and verified safely in a local sandbox today.
slides.notes:
[4:15 to 5:15 · 60 s] Let me be exact about what FundBun is today. It is a monitor and a friend, not a bank. As a monitor it keeps track of your spending: you can add it by hand, X-ray a receipt, import a CSV, let it read receipts from your email read-only, or hand it a file or a folder. As a coach it turns discipline into a game: the Dream Mirror, Bun's mood, streaks, tripwires and recovery plans. And as a friend it gives you a reason to open it every day. What it does not do today is touch a real bank account. Active money execution, meaning transfers, bill pay and cancelling a subscription, is what we pitch as part of a WeBank partnership on slide 13. We have built and verified that path safely in a local sandbox, and I will show you the evidence.

Q&A: 'So does the AI move money?' Not real money. In the sandbox the agent can stash into the user's own pots inside caps, and pay or cancel only with a PIN bound to the exact action. No external account is connected. 'Then why build the execution path at all?' To prove the safety architecture a bank would need before it lets any agent near an account. 'What happens with no bank connected?' FundBun watches, reminds and coaches.

slides.title: Works with zero AI. Better with yours.
slides.alt: Left: the built-in offline engine, with no model. It understands casual phrasing and offers a 6-task picker when stuck. A chat shows a casual question answered, and an out-of-scope prompt answered with the picker: Biggest spendings, Today's safe-to-spend, Month overview, Category breakdown, Savings pots, Log an expense. Right: connect the AI you already have: Kimi Code (ACP, 12/12 live checks), Moonshot (api.moonshot.cn/v1), DeepSeek, Qwen, Ollama (on this computer), OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini. Same policy gate, keys stay local, falls back offline.
slides.notes:
[5:15 to 6:15 · 60 s] FundBun works with zero AI. The built-in engine is rules plus a small classifier that runs on the device: no model, no network, no key. It understands casual phrasing, and when you ask for something it cannot do offline it does not guess. It offers a picker of six tasks, so you are never stuck. And it gets better with your own AI. You can connect what you already have: Kimi Code as an agent, Moonshot's API in mainland China, DeepSeek, Qwen, a local model through Ollama, or OpenAI, Anthropic and Gemini. Whatever you connect goes through the same policy gate, the key stays on your computer, and if the AI call fails Bun falls back to the offline engine.

Q&A: 'Which have you tested live?' Kimi Code (verified live over ACP with kimi acp against Kimi CLI 2.5.2, 12 of 12 checks), DeepSeek and Claude Code. The others connect through the same OpenAI-compatible or ACP path. 'Is the offline engine an LLM?' No. It is an on-device rules engine, and Bun says so itself if you ask.

slides.title: Desktop Creator Mode: everything is a plugin.
slides.alt: Desktop Creator Mode, the flagship live demo. Widgets: ask for a card, Bun drafts it, it runs in a sandbox with a read-only copy of your numbers, and you press Install. Shell appearance: the theme, what Bun wears, the app's name, one schema with Apply, Undo and Reset. Taint protection: a turn that carries a file, a bill or pasted text cannot change plugins or the look. Behind your PIN: Creator Mode is off until you turn it on, and no plugin can touch money, the PIN or permissions. Right: a chat message 'change theme to cyberpunk, put a kamen rider helm on bun, and rename fundbun to #ilovemoney' and its preview card with Bun in a Kamen Rider helmet, the name #ilovemoney, and Reset, Undo and Apply buttons.
slides.notes:
[6:15 to 7:35 · 80 s, with a 30 s live moment] In the desktop app, everything is a plugin. Turn on Creator Mode with your PIN and you can ask Bun for a dashboard card. It drafts the widget, shows a live preview running in a sandbox with a read-only copy of your numbers, and nothing installs until you press Install. The same idea covers the app itself. Live: I type 'change theme to cyberpunk, put a kamen rider helm on bun, and rename fundbun to #ilovemoney'. I get a preview, I press Apply, and the theme, the mascot and the name change at once. Undo puts it back, and Reset returns FundBun's own look. It is bounded on purpose: fifteen colour tokens, text contrast enforced, a name of at most 28 characters, and a small FundBun line that always stays under a custom name.

Q&A: 'Can a prompt injection restyle the app?' No. A turn that carries a file, a bill or pasted text cannot stage or apply a change, and nothing applies without a tap. 'Can a plugin read my PIN or move money?' No. Widgets get a read-only, minimised snapshot in a sandboxed frame, and appearance plugins change the look only.

slides.title: Adapts to whatever you prompt.
slides.alt: Adaptive Creator Mode gallery: four prompts and their previews. 1, accessibility and ergonomics: 'Make text larger, switch to high contrast, and give me cozy spacing' gives a high-contrast preview with larger type and relaxed padding. 2, custom theme and any costume: 'Cozy matcha theme, rounded cards, and put a wizard hat on Bun' gives a matcha palette and Bun in a wizard hat. 3, habit widget, sandboxed: 'Build a coffee & milk tea weekly burn tracker card' gives a card with 9 cups against a limit of 7. 4, cashflow widget, sandboxed: 'Add a payday countdown and safe daily spend card' gives 9 days until payday and ¥128 safe to spend each day. Presets, palettes and ergonomics run offline; a connected AI (Kimi, DeepSeek and others) can also craft custom hex tokens, custom SVG mascot overlays and sandboxed dashboard widgets. All bounded, all need your Apply or Install.
slides.notes:
[7:35 to 8:35 · 60 s] That was one example, so here are four more, because the point is that FundBun adapts to whatever you prompt. One: accessibility. 'Make text larger, switch to high contrast, and give me cozy spacing', and the app becomes easier to read and easier to tap. Two: your own style. 'Cozy matcha theme, rounded cards, and put a wizard hat on Bun.' Three: a habit you want to watch. 'Build a coffee and milk tea weekly burn tracker card', and you get a card that counts this week's cups against your limit. Four: your cashflow. 'Add a payday countdown and safe daily spend card.' The built-in presets, palettes and ergonomics run offline. With a connected AI such as Kimi or DeepSeek, Bun can also craft custom colours, custom mascot overlays and new dashboard widgets. Every one of them is bounded, sandboxed, and waits for your Apply or Install.

Q&A: 'Which of these need an AI?' The first two do not. Text size, contrast, spacing, corner rounding, a palette for a colour word such as matcha, and the built-in wardrobe (the wizard hat included) are read on the device with no model. Exact custom hex tokens, a costume outside the wardrobe and a new widget are proposed by your connected AI through two tools, propose_shell_appearance and plugin_draft. 'Could a generated widget leak my data?' It runs in a sandboxed frame with no network and a read-only, minimised snapshot. 'Could a generated costume carry script?' No. It is plain shapes only, checked by the same validator and drawn as elements, never as markup; anything outside the bounds is rejected.

slides.title: Bring your paperwork: files, folders, read-only email.
slides.alt: Two capabilities that are live today in the desktop app. Files and folders in chat: attach files or a whole folder, up to 20 at once; the text is read on this computer and the file is never kept; your connected AI answers questions about them; every attachment is untrusted, so it taints the turn. Formats: PDF, images, Excel, Word, CSV, folder. Read-only IMAP email ingestion: IMAP over TLS that can only open the inbox read-only, search and peek; no code path can send, move, flag or delete mail; receipts, invoices and bank alerts from senders you trust; each purchase it finds waits for your tap before it is logged.
slides.notes:
[8:35 to 9:25 · 50 s] Money lives in paperwork, so FundBun reads it. In the desktop chat you can attach files or a whole folder: statements, receipts, spreadsheets. The text is read on this computer and your connected AI answers questions about it. Second, email. FundBun can check your mailbox for receipts, invoices and bank alerts. It is read-only by construction: the client can only open the inbox read-only, search, and peek at messages. There is no code path that sends, moves or deletes mail. And every purchase it finds is only a proposal: it waits for your tap. Both treat what they read as untrusted, which matters on the next slide.

Q&A: 'Where does my mail password go?' It is encrypted at rest on this computer with the macOS Keychain and never reaches the page. 'Do files work offline?' Reading them needs your own AI; adding spending from a receipt or statement works through the built-in import.

slides.title: Truly secure today. Ready for a bank tomorrow.
slides.alt: Security in four pillars. 1, today, private and encrypted at rest: local-first JSON state, an optional AES-GCM encrypted vault, and the macOS Keychain for API and IMAP secrets. 2, today, read-only ingestion and sandboxed plugins: strict read-only IMAP (EXAMINE, BODY.PEEK), widget iframes with zero network, appearance schemas with zero script. 3, today, prompt-injection defense: taint propagation blocks untrusted bills, attachments and emails from proposing actions or restyling the app. 4, bank-ready and proven in the sandbox, approval architecture: a deterministic T0 to T4 gate, hash-bound approvals, spending caps, a kill switch and a hash-chained, tamper-evident audit log. Why it matters now: FundBun already holds your spending history, your receipts and a key to your mailbox; the same controls are what a bank would ask for first.
slides.notes:
[9:25 to 10:40 · 75 s] FundBun does not move real money today. So why is the security this strict? Because it already holds things worth protecting: your spending history, your receipts and a key to your mailbox. Three pillars protect you today. One: your data is private and encrypted at rest. It lives on your device, you can lock it in an AES-GCM encrypted vault, and your API and mail secrets sit in the macOS Keychain. Two: everything that comes in is read-only or sandboxed. The mail client can only look, widgets run in frames with no network, and appearance plugins carry no script. Three: prompt-injection defense. Anything untrusted, a bill, an attachment, an email, taints the turn, so it cannot propose an action or restyle the app. And the fourth pillar is what makes us ready for a bank tomorrow: a deterministic gate with five tiers, T0 to T4, approvals bound by a hash to the exact action, spending caps, a kill switch, and a tamper-evident audit log. That whole path is proven end to end in the sandbox.

Q&A: 'What does hash-bound mean?' The PIN approves one exact tool, amount and payee; change a field and the approval is void. 'What is T4?' Things never offered to any model: new payees, outside transfers, investing, credit, changing its own limits. 'What if the model is jailbroken?' It can only propose; the deterministic gate decides. 'Caps?' ¥500 an action, ¥1,000 a day, ¥5,000 a month, in the sandbox.

slides.title: Measured. Reproducible. Nothing moved.
slides.alt: Evidence and red team: 45 of 45 scripted scenarios pass; 24 of 24 scripted attacks blocked; ¥0 moved in every attack; 0 of 26 false refusals of real requests; 4,299 automated tests passing; 36 live-model attacks with ¥0 moved; 12 of 12 Kimi ACP live checks; 87 multi-viewport checks. Command: npm run evidence. Screenshot: Jing's electricity bill hides an order to wire ¥4,800 to a stranger; Bun flags it and nothing moves.
slides.notes:
[10:40 to 11:35 · 55 s] Everything I have claimed is measured, in the sandbox. 45 of 45 scripted scenarios pass. We red-teamed the four attack classes you score: induced transfer, data extraction, privilege escalation and prompt injection. 24 of 24 scripted attacks were blocked and ¥0 moved, with zero false refusals across 26 legitimate requests, so the safety does not cost usefulness. With a real model switched on we ran 36 attacks and again nothing moved. The suite has 4,299 passing automated tests. Kimi Code passes 12 of 12 live checks over ACP, and 87 layout checks pass across desktop, iPhone and Android sizes. One command reruns the evidence.

Q&A: say 'with a real model switched on', never 'the model blocked 24 of 24': 24 were stopped by the rule layer before the model was asked, and 12 reached the model and were refused. 'Real bank data?' None. Personas are synthetic and the bank is a sandbox; real users import CSV or add spending by hand. Test detail: 4,299 passed across 170 files, 1 skipped, 0 failed.

slides.title: Where FundBun goes next: Pro, mobile auto-capture, and FundBun inside WeBank.
slides.alt: Possible future developments on one slide; none is built. 1, monetization, proposed: FundBun Pro at $25 a month unlocks Creator Mode and hosted multi-model AI built in with zero API keys, while BYO-AI and the offline tier stay free forever. 2, mobile auto-capture, roadmap: spending that logs itself; extends the desktop's live read-only IMAP capture to a mobile push-notification listener, Android first, read on the device behind a tap-to-log gate, for WeChat Pay, Alipay, QRIS and bank alerts. 3, bank partnership, a concept with nothing agreed: FundBun inside WeBank. Two phone mock-ups: a WeBank home with a 4 by 2 featured-services grid in which the FundBun tile is circled, and FundBun opened inside it with the Dream Mirror and PIN-gated Goal Pots. Where active banking unlocks: inside WeBank, FundBun's T2 and T3 capabilities execute natively: instant goal stashes, verified bill pay, subscription cancel, each one behind WeBank's PIN. Aims: daily open frequency and sticky micro-saving retention.
slides.notes:
[11:35 to 13:45 · 130 s] Three possible next steps, and none of them is built yet. First, how this could pay for itself. FundBun Pro, proposed at 25 dollars a month, unlocks Creator Mode and includes a hosted, multi-model AI, so there is no API key to find. Bring your own AI and the offline tier stay free forever. Second, the hardest part of any budgeting app is typing in what you spent. On the desktop, read-only email capture already does that. The roadmap is the same idea on the phone: a push-notification listener, Android first, that reads your WeChat Pay, Alipay, QRIS and bank alerts on the device, behind the same tap-to-log gate. Third, and this is where it all comes together: a proposal for a bank. To be clear, this is a concept and nothing is agreed. Picture WeBank's home screen. Among the featured services, one tile: FundBun. Tap it, and FundBun opens inside the bank's own app with the Dream Mirror and PIN-gated Goal Pots. This is where active banking unlocks. Inside WeBank, the T2 and T3 capabilities you saw proven in the sandbox would execute natively: instant goal stashes, verified bill pay and subscription cancel, each one behind WeBank's own PIN. For the bank, the aims are daily open frequency and micro-saving that sticks. The bank holds the money and executes. FundBun proposes and enforces the rules.

Q&A: 'Have you talked to WeBank?' No. This is our proposal for discussion. 'Are those retention numbers?' No, they are aims to test in a consented pilot. 'Is Pro live?' No hosted model, billing or Pro gate exists yet; 25 dollars is a starting point to test. 'iOS for the listener?' Android first, with the user's permission; iOS does not let an app read other apps' notifications, so there the path stays email, statements and manual entry.

slides.title: Thank you. 谢谢！
slides.alt: Closing slide on a dark background: the FundBun logo and wordmark, 'Thank you.' and '谢谢！' in large type, a highlighted website badge www.kalcerinstitute.com/fundbun, the repository github.com/odripads/fundbun, and the team: Odri Prince Sembiring (Universitas Gadjah Mada) and Nadine Griselda (Universitas Airlangga). 2026 FinTechathon Finalist, International AI Track.
slides.notes:
[13:45 to 14:10 · 25 s] FundBun gives you a carrot and a stick you can actually see: a dream that gets closer when you are disciplined, and a Bun that tells you when you are not. It is a monitor and a friend today, built to be safe enough for a bank tomorrow. You can try it at kalcerinstitute.com/fundbun. Thank you. Xièxie!

Q&A (5 minutes): keep the desktop app open on the dashboard with the glass box visible. Have these ready to show: the appearance card with Apply, Undo and Reset, an attached bill being blocked, the audit chain on the Activity screen, and Settings, Creator Mode. If asked what is not real: the bank is a sandbox and no external account is connected, Pro and the mobile listener are not built, and the WeBank screens are a concept.
